items.summary: In this week’s South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna discuss the aftermath of the Jantar Mantar protests, led by the Cockroach Janta Party. They are joined by senior journalist and editor of The Wire, Seema Chisti, and Peek TV co-founder Vedanta Agarwal. Seema Chisti begins by commenting on the government’s denial of the use of pellet guns and violence on the protestors. “The government keeps denying this, but we must also take note. The CRPF chief was quoted as saying to go for the protests fearlessly. But I am unsure what that means with the government using force nonetheless. The government also seems to unleash a lot of demonstrative brutality on all kinds of protests across the country. This is to show how people who raise dissent will be treated. But this generation is not typical in the sense that they come from all parts of the political spectrum, and that is also confusing and scaring the government,” she says. Vedanta says that now we are seeing an outreach to Gen Z by the government. “We see politicians use Gen Z words in Parliament as well. items.title: Masking number plate of vehicle a violation under MV Act but not cheating under IPC: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently quashed a cheating case against a man who was booked for riding a scooter with its rear number plate covered by a black mask [ Mohammed Abdul Ahad Shaker v. State of Telangana ]. In an order passed on July 28, a Bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih held that merely obstructing a vehicle's number plate would not constitute the offence of cheating under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) unless the essential ingredients of the offence are established. The Court clarified that covering the number plate of a vehicle could amount to a regulatory violation under the Motor Vehicles Act (MV Act) but such a violation could not be converted into a cheating offence. “ The regulatory breach of obstructing the number plate under the MV Act and rules thereunder cannot be dressed as an offence under Section 420 of the IPC without establishing the essential ingredients as required, ” the Court said. items.title: क्या थार बन गई है 'मर्दानगी' का सिंबल? लड़कियों ने क्या कहा
items.summary: थार सिर्फ एक गाड़ी नहीं रह गई है. भारत के कई शहरों और कस्बों में यह एक खास तरह के वर्चस्व का प्रतीक बनती जा रही है. सोशल मीडिया पर थार के वीडियो देखें तो अक्सर एक पैटर्न दिखाई देता है. तेज रफ्तार, खतरनाक स्टंट, ट्रैफिक नियमों की अनदेखी और इन सबके साथ एक आक्रामक रवैया भी थार और उसके मालिकों की छवि से जुड़ा है. बड़ी गाड़ी, ऊंची सीट और दमदार इंजन कुछ लोगों के लिए सुविधा का नहीं, बल्कि सड़क पर वर्चस्व दिखाने का माध्यम बन जाते हैं. कई बार यह व्यवहार उस पुरुषवादी सोच से भी जुड़ जाता है जिसमें आक्रामकता को मर्दानगी का प्रतीक माना जाता है. मानो थार महज एक गाड़ी नहीं, बल्कि ‘मर्द होने’ का एक स्टेटमेंट हो. लेकिन असल सवाल यह है कि महिलाएं थार के बारे में क्या सोचती हैं? क्या वो थार चलाने वालों को जज करती हैं? क्या बड़ी गाड़ी सचमुच किसी की पर्सनैलिटी को ज्यादा आकर्षक बना देती है? क्या आक्रामक ड्राइविंग को महिलाएं आत्मविश्वास समझती हैं या असुरक्षा की निशानी? क्या सड़क पर दबंगई दिखाना प्रभाव छोड़ता है या नकारात्मक छवि बनाता है? और सबसे अहम, क्या थार की लोकप्रिय छवि पुरुषों की कल्पना है या महिलाओं की भी यही राय है? इस वीडियो में हम इन्हीं सवालो का जवाब जानने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं. पल्टीमार नेताओं पर जनता ने क्या कहा? राम मंदिर में चंदा चोरी: किसे जिम्मेदार मानती है जनता?

items.title: Punjab spending large amount of money on freebies, ads but not paying dues to employees: P&H High Court
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Monday observed that the Punjab government was spending huge amounts of money on freebies and advertisements but withholding legitimate dues of its own employees citing financial constraints. A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor made the observation in a judgment directing Punjab government to release up-to-date pending installments of dearness allowance/ dearness relief (DA/DR) to all its employees and pensioners. The Court also said that Punjab shall not resort to any unproductive expenditures such as large-scale advertising campaigns in print or social media, till these dues are cleared. "While the issue of financial constraints is being raised as a ground for withholding the legitimate dues of the State’s own employees, however, as per the information available in the public domain, the State is expending large amounts of money on grant of freebies, doles, advertorial campaigns, and other expenditure, which would not strictly fall within the domain of essential expenditure by a welfare State, cannot be brushed aside, lightly," the Court said. items.title: ‘Feels like career over’: The online campaign to intimidate women part of CJP protest
items.summary: A BJP MLA posts a video of a bleeding, weeping girl and tells his followers she is being taught a lesson. The video is actually from Varanasi, from a domestic violence case, and has nothing to do with the protest. It does not matter. The comments say: she didn’t get beaten enough . In the two weeks since the Cockroach Janata Party’s July 20 Parliament march, more than half a dozen women and girls who appeared in clips from CJP protests have been identified across X, Instagram and Facebook – by an elected legislator, by Hindutva handles with large followings, by strangers who have sought to file police complaints and published home addresses. They face threats of rape and death. There are other consequences too. A yoga instructor has lost many of her clients, a widowed mother has lost her tuition work, a teenager’s family home stands locked. The case that has drawn the most television attention is that of Ruchika Singh, a 15-year-old filmed at Jantar Mantar using expletives against Prime Minister Modi, who now faces charges of defamation and “intentional insult to provoke breach of peace”.
